text: Mangwon Market, 5:47 on Tuesday evening. Shoppers stampede as eyeless ash hounds pour in.
Seoa is in there, dragging a crying boy into a rice-cake shop, and Jaeha had better listen: stay off the main street.
With two market grannies, she herds a dozen people into the back and drops the shutter.
A hound hits it so hard the metal bulges. Seoa braces it with her shoulder.
She's already thinking. Come in by the pharmacy alley. It's too narrow for two hounds.
Jaeha runs flat out, still bloody from the tower, with Borro cracking the pavement behind him.
He begs her to get up on a roof. She refuses. People are still in the fish lane.
Seoa has never waited to be rescued. She isn't starting tonight.
At the pharmacy alley, police fumble with tape as a Gate Rescue van screeches onto the kerb.
Out jumps Choi, exasperated. Of course it's Jaeha.
The hunters are fifteen minutes out. Black Hound held this gate's contract, and postponed it twice.
Good news: a break floods the street with gate mana, so summon cooldowns drop from four hours to one minute.
Phones film from behind the tape. Jaeha doesn't care. He closes his notebook. Summons go first. Finally, an order Nib likes.
Field form for both: full power on a five-minute clock.
Nib cuts a leaping hound in half in mid-air.
Bomi skids up: what does he need? Her drone, up high, so he can see the whole market.
From above: one covered street, alleys like ribs, packs of hounds, knots of people.
Seoa adds the catch: the fish lane's only exit is the footbridge.
Jaeha sees it. Every alley is one hound wide. Funnel them into one square, and they reach Borro one at a time.
Through the link, he whispers his orders. Borro holds the square. Nib drives the hounds to him.
Borro plants himself in the square, and his shield fills the alley wall to wall.
The hounds come single file and smash into the iron, one after another.
Each hit lands in Jaeha's body too. That's Carry: he takes a quarter of Borro's damage himself.
Nib runs the stall awnings and drops on the hounds, herding them to the square.
One hound slips past toward the shop full of children. The tall kimchi granny in her red rubber apron blocks its way.
She swings a giant radish like a baseball bat. Not in her alley.
Nib drops from above and finishes the dazed hound with one knife.
He gives her a solemn nod. Good swing, grandmother. She has more radishes. Go!
In the fish lane, Seoa leads a chain of people out hand in hand, counting heads. Fourteen.
Yerin heals a bitten leg, whispering that she is not freezing. Choi runs past carrying an old woman.
Two hounds hit Borro from two alleys at once. Shield for one, stone shell for the other.
Carrying for two summons, Jaeha starts to bleed from the nose. The load hits ninety percent.
Forty-eight thousand are watching Bomi's stream. The chat says that husk is a tank.
Under the fish lane, violet light pours up the stairs, and the ice on the stalls melts.
Then a second wave boils out of the gate, twenty hounds or more.
And they're heading for the footbridge, where Seoa's line has just started to climb.
Jaeha screams across the market: fall back to the stairs!
Borro ploughs down the main street like a battering ram, with Nib running the awnings above.
Seoa's people are halfway across the footbridge, and the flood is right behind them.
Nib lands on the top step to face the whole pack alone. A wall again. Fine.
The stairs fit two hounds at a time, and Nib cuts down every pair.
Then the road under the bridge bulges up, steaming and glowing violet.
A crack races up the bridge's only pier.
The deck sags. People scream and grab the railings, and Seoa holds a child tight.
Jaeha sees his sister on a falling bridge. Borro, the pier!
Borro leaps onto the buckling road and runs underneath.
The pier gives way, and Borro catches the bridge. Shell to the concrete, shield against the pier, feet sunk in the road, he holds the deck with Seoa still on it.
Its weight lands on Jaeha too. He drops to one knee. One hundred and sixty percent. Overload.
Borro once carried a village across a bridge. Today he's carrying the bridge.
Seoa walks backwards across the tilted deck, a child on her hip. Don't run, and don't stop.
Under the concrete, Borro is sweating, but calm. Take your time, little ones. He's slow on purpose.
On the stairs, Nib's outline flickers. Eight seconds of field form left.
It ends just as a hound leaps. Rest form: no stronger than an ordinary person, with a minute of cooldown.
The hound flattens him. One knife skitters away, and he holds its jaws off with the other.
So Bomi sends her drone screaming straight at it. Sorry, baby. Mommy will buy you a new one.
The drone explodes against the hound and knocks it off Nib, down the stairs.
The stream dies with nearly fifty-two thousand watching. The chat mourns the drone.
The hounds climb again, and Nib still has twelve seconds of cooldown.
Then Choi blasts an extinguisher in their faces, and the kimchi granny swings another radish.
Twelve seconds, bought. Jaeha raises a bloody hand, and Nib gets five more minutes.
Nib's eye flares amber, and he tears out of the white cloud, bursting hounds into ash.
Seoa steps off the far end with the last child. Borro asks: everyone off? All fourteen!
Only then does Borro step out, and the footbridge crashes down behind him, empty.
The dust settles. Across the gap, Seoa stands in front of her fourteen people.
She holds a plastic bag high and shouts across the gap. She got the rice cakes.
Jaeha laughs in spite of himself, one bloody hand over his eyes.
But the steam from the road is getting thicker, and the cracks are glowing violet.
Choi wipes his neck. Why is it so hot? It's October.
The laugh dies on Jaeha's face.
The road under the wreck swells into a dome, and Borro backs away, shield up.
And the break's boss bursts out of the street: a colossal jade-and-gold serpent, horned and hooded, rearing three storeys high.
One yellow slit eye, and a warning. Break boss: Marsh Serpent, C-grade.
